card.name: Trigger words in stop-treatment conditions
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as who, if, any, or and of that open a condition clause, after patients or after a stop or continue instruction. They come right before a named reaction or finding.

modes.label: Who/any after patients
modes.description: The word who or any follows patients and introduces the reaction that triggers stopping the drug.
modes.example: Treatment should be suspended in any patient<< who>> develops clinical or laboratory findings suggestive of l

modes.label: If/regardless of
modes.description: Conditional or concessive words follow a dosing instruction and lead into a circumstance.
modes.example: Continue treatment for the full 7 days, even<< if>> there is improvement.

modes.label: Or/of inside condition phrase
modes.description: A linking word sits inside a phrase listing signs or circumstances.
modes.example: Consider treatment interruption in patients who develop signs<< or>> symptoms of acute myocardial ischemia.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward the word conditions or condition, as in a circumstance clause.
card.plain: It marks the small word that opens a 'if this happens' clause in label instructions.
